C-2.gap: User-spec says 'lives only in JS memory of WKWebView'. Tech-spec correctly places the canonical tree in Swift (InsightSession/InsightNode). Decision 3 does not acknowledge or resolve this divergence from user-spec wording. The user-facing constraint (no DB, no cross-session) is met, but the tech-spec should note that 'JS memory' in user-spec was an implementation assumption the team refined — canonical tree is Swift-side, JS holds only rendered snapshots. Minor, as intent is satisfied.

findings.detail: Decision 11 §3 prescribes session.retryCurrent() as the retry entry point. Task 4 mandates its implementation. But the canonical InsightSession data model (Data Models section, method list) does not include retryCurrent() or handleStreamError — only: generateRoot, expand(deepDiveIndex:), navigateTo, up, cancel, currentNode(), breadcrumbs(), snapshot(). A developer implementing from the data model interface would miss both methods. The authoritative interface definition must be kept in sync with behavioral prescriptions. Adding a method in Decision prose without updating the interface listing is the classic 'decision scattered across sections' anti-pattern.

findings.requirement: Architecture section: WebViewBridge bridge message counts
findings.detail: Architecture section (What we're building/modifying, WebViewBridge.swift entry) still reads: 'add 4 Swift→JS commands' and 'Add 4 JS→Swift message types'. Task 6 correctly describes 5 Swift→JS commands (loadInsightView, appendInsightDelta, setInsightDeepDives, showInsightLoading, setInsightError) and 5 JS→Swift message types (insightDeepDiveClicked, insightSaveRequested, insightBreadcrumbClicked, insightUpClicked, insightRetryRequested). The Architecture section is the document-level summary that readers and reviewers consult first. Having it say '4' while Task 6 says '5' creates implementation-time ambiguity — a developer reading Architecture would implement 4 message types and miss setInsightError and insightRetryRequested, which are the entire retry error-recovery path.

findings.requirement: C-2: Tree lives only in JS memory of WKWebView
findings.detail: User-spec explicitly says 'lives only in JS memory of WKWebView, not saved to SQLite'. The actual design stores the canonical tree in Swift (InsightSession, InsightNode as reference types). JS holds only rendered snapshots per navigateTo call. Decision 3 does not acknowledge this divergence. A future reader comparing user-spec to tech-spec will encounter a contradiction without explanation. Decision 3 should explicitly note that 'JS memory' in user-spec was an implementation assumption refined during tech design — the user-facing constraint (no DB, no cross-session persistence) is met by Swift-side ARC lifecycle. Low severity because user intent is satisfied.

findings.requirement: Streaming pipeline: setInsightDeepDives and showInsightLoading trigger conditions unspecified
findings.detail: The streaming pipeline diagram (Architecture section) shows JS handles topic rendering autonomously — the ---DEEP-DIVES--- marker parser triggers right-pane rendering inline during appendInsightDelta processing. Neither setInsightDeepDives nor showInsightLoading appears in the streaming pipeline diagram. No task description, no Decision, and no Acceptance Criteria bullet specifies when Swift would call setInsightDeepDives (given JS already renders topics from the marker) or when showInsightLoading fires relative to appendInsightDelta. Task 6 lists them as commands to implement but provides no trigger condition. These two commands risk becoming dead scaffolding — implemented in Task 6, never called. The spec should either (a) define a specific trigger for each command with a code path that invokes it, or (b) remove them and confirm JS autonomously handles loading state and topic rendering.

summary: 10/11 requirements covered, 1 partial (C-2: tree location language mismatch with user-spec, minor). Previous major issues G-2/UE-1, UE-2, UE-3 are resolved or substantially addressed. Two new critical structural gaps introduced by iteration-1 edits: F-1 — InsightSession data model interface is missing retryCurrent() and handleStreamError methods that Decision 11 §3 and Task 4 prescribe (developer implementing from data model would miss the entire retry path); F-2 — Architecture section still says '4 Swift→JS commands' and '4 JS→Swift message types' while Task 6 correctly specifies 5 of each (setInsightError and insightRetryRequested are the error-recovery path added in this iteration). Two minor findings remain: F-3 (G-3 carry-forward: user-spec says JS memory, spec uses Swift memory, no reconciliation note) and F-4 (OE-1 carry-forward: setInsightDeepDives and showInsightLoading have no specified trigger condition in the streaming pipeline). Status: FAIL — 2 critical findings.
